newsitem.title: USA: US V.P. Gore reaffirms commitment to low inflation.
newsitem.headline: US V.P. Gore reaffirms commitment to low inflation.

text.p: U.S. Vice President Al Gore Tuesday reaffirmed America's commitment to low inflation and open markets.

Addressing the plenary session of International Monetary Fund/World Bank annual meeting, Gore said the United States has enjoyed strong, steady economic growth that has helped to reduce poverty and slash the federal budget deficit.
"Growth and openness here at home coupled with growth and openness abroad has been good for America," Gore said.

Gore, who has criticized the World Bank and other multilateral development banks in the past for not doing enough to protect the environment, welcomed the progress that has been made on that front recently.
"I welcome the great distance that has been travelled," he said. But, he added, "The really hard work now remains."

He also stressed the importance of "good government" -- government that is fully representative, transparent, accountable and restrained. "Good government is the key to equitable and sustainable growth," he said.
Gore urged the IMF and the World Bank to focus selectively on the areas where they can make a difference. "As they evolve, they must be as modern as the markets they serve," he said.
He pledged that the Clinton administration would "do all in our power" to meet America's commitment to funding the World Bank's International Development Association.
The United States is behind on its payments to IDA as the Congress has refused to provide all the financing the administration has requested.
